mainTopic: תרומה rules for people who are left out, giving women their turn first, and the mixed-up sons of a כהן and a slave
overview: The גמרא explains a ברייתא that lists people who do not get a share of תרומה at the threshing floor, and gives a reason for each one. For an אשה, רב פפא and רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע disagree: one says the worry is a hidden גרושה, the other says it is יחוד. The גמרא shows where those two reasons lead to different rulings. It then explains why תרומה may be sent home to a ערל but not to a טמא: the ערל is much more truly forced into his condition. A second ברייתא teaches that a woman is served first when מעשר עני is given out, to spare her embarrassment, and רבא tells how this led him to hear women's court cases first. Back in the משנה, רבא says the mixed-up sons are forced to free each other so that they can marry. The משנה's rule that 'the stringencies of both' apply to them is explained as being about their מנחה: a קמיצה is taken, the rest is not eaten, and in the end the שיריים are scattered on the בית הדשן according to all opinions. Finally, a new משנה begins about a son whose father is unknown, ruling that he and his half-brothers do חליצה but not יבום.

steps.title: The easy reasons for most of the list
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes listing the obvious reasons why several types of people are not given תרומה at the threshing floor.
steps.simpleTranslation: טומטום and אנדרוגינוס are a separate kind of person. An עבד is also understood: if he gets תרומה, people may later treat him as a כהן by lineage. A ערל and a טמא are left out because it is unpleasant. One who marries a woman forbidden to him is left out as a penalty.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is going down the list in the ברייתא and giving the simple reason for each person. This is the setup: these cases are clear, so the next step can ask about the one case that is not clear.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each person gets his own reason. For the עבד the worry is a chain: getting תרומה in public could be taken as proof that he is a כהן, and that could affect his family's lineage (יוחסין). The ערל and the טמא are not losing their right to תרומה; it is just not proper to hand it to them in public. The one who married a forbidden woman loses it as a קנס.

keyTerms.meaning: A creature of its own kind, a separate category
To raise someone to the status of proper lineage
Because they are repulsive or unpleasant
A woman who is not fit for him to marry

steps.confusionAlert: The ערל and the טמא are not being told they have no right to תרומה. The issue is only that handing it to them in public is improper.

phrases.english: they are a creature of their own kind.
phrases.notes: "They" are the טומטום and the אנדרוגינוס, mentioned just before this in the גמרא.

phrases.english: A slave is also understood:
perhaps they will come to raise him
from eating teruma to having priestly lineage.
An uncircumcised man and an impure man:
because they are repulsive.
One who marries a woman unfit for him:
because of a penalty.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the list of simple reasons that the גמרא started before this section.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Each excluded person has a clear reason: separate category, lineage worry, unpleasantness, or penalty.

steps.title: Why is a woman left out?
steps.stepSummary: Unlike the others, the reason for leaving out an אשה is not obvious, so the גמרא asks for it.
steps.simpleTranslation: But a woman: why is she not given a share?
steps.whatsHappening: After explaining everyone else, the גמרא asks about the one case left: an אשה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A כהן's daughter or wife may eat תרומה, so it is not clear why she is excluded from the public sharing. None of the earlier reasons fits her. The word אלא shows this case is different from the ones just explained.

phrases.english: But a woman,
what is the reason she is not given?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follows the list of clear cases and points to the one unclear case.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The reason an אשה is not given תרומה at the threshing floor.

steps.title: Two reasons: divorce or being alone
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא and רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע disagree. One says the worry is a גרושה, the other says the worry is יחוד.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא and רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע disagree. One says: because of a divorced woman. The other says: because of being alone together.
steps.whatsHappening: Two אמוראים each give a different reason why an אשה is not given תרומה in public.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By the first view, a woman who ate תרומה through marriage to a כהן may have been divorced and lost that right, and the giver would not know. So no women get it, to protect against that. By the second view, the problem is that the owner and the woman might end up alone together at the threshing floor.

keyTerms.meaning: A man and woman being alone together

phrases.english: Rav Pappa disagrees about it
with Rav Huna, son of Rav Yehoshua.
One said: because of a divorcée.
And one said: because of being alone together.

steps.triggerLanguage: פְּלִיגִי בַּהּ רַב פָּפָּא וְרַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוֹשֻׁעַ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question about an אשה with two competing reasons.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Either the worry of a hidden גרושה or the worry of יחוד.

steps.title: What difference do the two reasons make?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks where the two reasons would lead to different rulings.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the difference between them?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for a real case where the two reasons give different answers. This sets up the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both reasons lead to the same rule, that women are not given תרומה. So the גמרא wants a case where one reason applies and the other does not.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the practical difference between them?

phrases.english: What is the difference between them?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks how the two opinions of step 3 differ in practice.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A case where the גרושה reason and the יחוד reason lead to different results.

steps.title: Near but empty, or far but busy
steps.stepSummary: The reasons differ for a threshing floor close to town that few people visit, and for one far away that many people visit.
steps.simpleTranslation: The difference is a threshing floor near town that few people come to. Or one that is far away but many people come to.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives two cases where only one of the two reasons applies.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Near town, the owner would hear if she was divorced, so the גרושה worry is gone. But with few people around, the יחוד worry remains. Far from town, the owner might not know about a divorce, so the גרושה worry applies. But with many people around, there is no יחוד worry.
steps.whatToRemember: Distance from town affects the גרושה worry, because news of a divorce travels. How crowded the place is affects the יחוד worry.

phrases.english: The difference between them is a threshing floor
that is close to town,
but people are not found there.
Alternatively: one that is far away,
but people are found there.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיכָּא בֵּינַיְיהוּ בֵּי דָרֵי דִּמְקָרַב לְמָתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 4 with two cases.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Near and empty: only יחוד applies. Far and busy: only גרושה applies.

steps.title: תרומה may be sent home, with two exceptions
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next line of the ברייתא: all these people may have תרומה sent to their homes, except a טמא and one who married a forbidden woman.
steps.simpleTranslation: And to all of them we send it to their homes, except a ritually impure man and one who marries a woman unfit for him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the next line of the ברייתא it is studying. This sets up the question in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Being left out in public does not mean losing תרומה completely. Sending it privately is allowed for most of the list. Only the טמא and the one being penalized do not receive it even at home.

phrases.english: And to all of them, we send it to their homes,
except for an impure man
and one who marries a woman unfit for him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from public sharing to the ברייתא's rule about sending תרומה home.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: תרומה may be sent home to all those listed except a טמא and one who married a forbidden woman.

steps.title: Why may it be sent to an uncircumcised man?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא notes that a ערל is not among the exceptions, so it may be sent to him, and asks why he differs from a טמא.
steps.simpleTranslation: But to an uncircumcised man we do send it. What is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא draws an inference from the ברייתא and asks for the reason behind it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Back in step 1, the ערל and the טמא were grouped together as unpleasant. Yet here the טמא is excluded even at home and the ערל is not. So the גמרא asks what makes the ערל different.

phrases.english: But to an uncircumcised man, we send it to him;
what is the reason?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲבָל עָרֵל מְשַׁגְּרִינַן לֵיהּ, מַאי טַעְמָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws an inference from the ברייתא in step 6 and questions it in light of step 1.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why a ערל may have תרומה sent home when a טמא may not.

steps.title: The ערל gets תרומה because he cannot help it
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that a ערל may have תרומה sent to him because his state is forced on him.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because he is forced into it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from step 7: a ערל may have תרומה sent home because he did not choose to stay uncircumcised.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This ערל is someone for whom מילה would be dangerous, so he is held back from it by force of circumstance. Because it is not his fault, he is not pushed away from getting תרומה.

keyTerms.meaning: Someone forced by circumstances beyond his control

phrases.english: Because he is forced by circumstances.
phrases.notes: This is the ערל whose brothers died from their מילה, so he is not allowed to risk it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 7
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A ערל is אנוס, so it is not his fault and he may receive תרומה at home

steps.title: But a טמא is also forced
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges: a טמא also became impure without choosing to, so why is he left out?
steps.simpleTranslation: A טמא is also forced, isn't he?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the answer: if being forced is the reason, a טמא should also count as forced.
steps.deeperAnalysis: People often become impure without meaning to. If that is so, being אנוס should help the טמא as well, and the difference between him and the ערל is gone again.

keyTerms.meaning: A person who is ritually impure

phrases.english: An impure person too, isn't he forced?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of step 8
steps.kashyaTarget: The reasoning that being אנוס explains why a ערל gets תרומה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A טמא is also usually אנוס, so the same reason should apply to him too

steps.title: The ערל is much more forced than the טמא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the ערל is completely forced, but the טמא is not forced to the same degree.
steps.simpleTranslation: This one is very much forced, and that one is not very much forced.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the two cases are not equal: the ערל's situation is far more out of his control than the טמא's.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For the ערל, מילה could put his life in danger, so he truly has no choice. A טמא could have been more careful to avoid becoming impure, so his situation is less forced.

keyTerms.meaning: His situation is very much forced on him

steps.whatToRemember: A ערל may have תרומה sent home because his condition is completely forced on him. A טמא may not, because he is less forced.

phrases.english: This one, his being forced is great,
and this one, his being forced is not great.

steps.triggerLanguage: הַאי נְפִישׁ אוּנְסֵיהּ, וְהַאי לָא נְפִישׁ אוּנְסֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 9
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both the ערל and the טמא are equally אנוס
steps.terutzMaskana: The ערל is fully אנוס because of danger. The טמא is less so, because he could have guarded himself.

steps.title: A ברייתא about a slave and a woman at the threshing floor
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says not to give תרומה to a slave or a woman at the threshing floor, and that where things are given out, the woman goes first.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: a slave and a woman are not given a share of תרומה at the threshing floors. And in a place where they do give out, the woman is given first and sent off right away.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ברייתא about giving out gifts to a slave and a woman.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא has two parts. First, these people are not given תרומה at the threshing floor. Second, where giving does happen, the woman is served first. The second part seems to clash with the first, which sets up the next question.

keyTerms.meaning: The threshing floors, where grain is processed and gifts are given out

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
The slave and the woman,
we do not give out תרומה to them
at the threshing floors.
And in a place where they do give out,
they give to the woman first
and send her off right away.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: הָעֶבֶד וְהָאִשָּׁה, אֵין חוֹלְקִין לָהֶם תְּרוּמָה בְּבֵית הַגֳּרָנוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new ברייתא on a related topic of giving out gifts
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A slave and a woman are not given תרומה at the threshing floor. Where things are given out, the woman is served first and sent off quickly.

steps.title: What does the ברייתא mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how the ברייתא can talk about a place where they give to her, right after saying they do not.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is it saying?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out that the ברייתא seems to contradict itself and asks what it really means.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first line says not to give a woman תרומה at the threshing floor. The second line speaks of a place where they do give to her. These two lines do not seem to fit together.

keyTerms.meaning: What is it saying? (the text seems unclear or self-contradicting)

phrases.english: What is it saying?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the wording of the ברייתא in step 11
steps.kashyaTarget: The second line of the ברייתא
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: It says they do not give to her, then speaks of a place where they do give

steps.title: The second line is about מעשר עני
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that the second line of the ברייתא is about giving out מעשר עני, not תרומה.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what it is saying: in a place where they give out מעשר עני, they give to the woman first.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the second half of the ברייתא is talking about a different gift, מעשר עני.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once the second line is about מעשר עני, there is no clash anymore. A woman is not given תרומה at the threshing floor, but when מעשר עני is given out, she is served first.

keyTerms.meaning: The tithe given to the poor

phrases.english: This is what it is saying:
In a place where they give out the poor man's tithe,
they give to the woman first.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָכִי קָאָמַר: בְּמָקוֹם שֶׁחוֹלְקִין מַעְשַׂר עָנִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 12
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reading the line as being about a different subject
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The whole ברייתא is about תרומה, so it contradicts itself
steps.terutzMaskana: The second line is about מעשר עני, where the woman is served first

steps.title: Why the woman goes first: to spare her embarrassment
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the woman is served first and answers that it is to keep her from being embarrassed.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason? Because of embarrassment.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks and right away answers why the woman is given מעשר עני first.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Waiting a long time in a crowd of men would be embarrassing for her. Serving her first lets her leave quickly.

keyTerms.meaning: Embarrassment, something that lowers a person's dignity

phrases.english: What is the reason?
Because of embarrassment.
phrases.notes: He means it is undignified for her to stand waiting among the men.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the reason for the rule in step 13
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: She is served first so she will not be embarrassed by waiting among men

steps.title: רבא changes the order of hearing court cases
steps.stepSummary: רבא says he used to hear a man's case first, but after learning this ברייתא he heard the woman's case first.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: At first, when a man and a woman came before me for judgment, I would settle the man's case first. I said: he is obligated in מצוות. Once I heard this, I settle the woman's case first. What is the reason? Because of embarrassment.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא tells how this ברייתא changed the way he ran his court.
steps.deeperAnalysis: At first רבא let the man go first so he could get back to his many מצוות. After he learned the ברייתא, he took the woman first, so she would not be embarrassed by waiting among men. The same reason of זילותא now applies to court cases too.
steps.whatToRemember: A woman is served first when gifts are given out, and רבא heard women's court cases first. The reason is to spare her embarrassment (זילותא).
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows a ברייתא about giving out gifts being used as a guide for how a בית דין should act.

phrases.english: Rava said:
At first,
when a man and a woman would come
for judgment before me,
I would settle the man's dispute first.
I said: since he is obligated in מצוות.
phrases.notes: He means: don't hold up a man who has more מצוות to go do.

phrases.english: Once I heard this,
I settle the woman's dispute first.
What is the reason? Because of embarrassment.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: מֵרֵישָׁא, כִּי הֲווֹ אָתוּ גַּבְרָא וְאִתְּתָא לְדִינָא קַמַּאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the reason from step 14 to court cases
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A judge should hear a woman's case before a man's, so she will not be embarrassed by waiting

steps.title: The mixed-up sons grew up and freed each other
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה and reads from its past-tense wording that freeing each other seems to be optional.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says: if the mixed-up sons grew up and freed each other, they may marry. 'Freed' sounds like it happened on its own. So if one wants to, fine, and if he doesn't want to, he doesn't have to.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the משנה about the mixed-up sons and points out what its wording seems to imply. This sets up the question that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says 'שיחררו' (they freed), in the past tense. That sounds like it only describes what happens if they chose to do it. The גמרא draws out the inference that it is up to each son.

keyTerms.meaning: The mixed-up ones: the son of the כהן's wife and the son of her שפחה, and no one knows which is which

phrases.english: If the mixed-up ones grew up, etc.
phrases.notes: This quotes our משנה: the son of a כהן's wife got mixed up with her שפחה's son.

phrases.english: 'They freed': if he wants, yes,
phrases.notes: The past tense makes it sound like this only describes what happens if they chose to free each other.

phrases.english: if he does not want, no.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns from the side discussion about תרומה and women to the next line of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The wording 'שיחררו' implies that freeing each other is optional.

steps.title: Why should it be optional when they cannot marry anyone?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the idea that freeing each other is optional. In their current state, neither son can marry a שפחה or a free woman.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why not force them? He cannot marry a שפחה, and he cannot marry a free woman!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the reading from the last step. Leaving the sons unable to marry anyone makes no sense.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each son might be a כהן, so he cannot marry a שפחה. Each might also be a slave, so he cannot marry a בת חורין. If freeing each other were optional, they could be stuck forever with no way to marry.

phrases.english: But why?
He cannot marry a maidservant,
and he cannot marry a free woman!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the inference drawn in step 16.
steps.kashyaTarget: The inference that freeing each other is optional
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If it were optional, the sons would be left unable to marry anyone, so they should be required to free each other.

steps.title: רבא: we force them to free each other
steps.stepSummary: רבא rereads the משנה: בית דין forces the sons to free each other.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: read the משנה as saying, 'We force them, and they free each other.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers the challenge by changing how we read the משנה. Freeing each other is not optional; they are forced to do it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The past tense 'שיחררו' is not meant to say it is up to them. רבא reads it as 'we force them, and they free each other'. That solves the problem of the sons being unable to marry.

keyTerms.meaning: Say / read it as (a rereading of the text)

steps.whatToRemember: The mixed-up sons are forced to free each other so that they can marry.

phrases.english: Rava said: say,
we force them,
and they free each other.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 17.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereading the wording of the משנה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The past tense means freeing each other is optional.
steps.terutzMaskana: בית דין forces them to free each other.

steps.title: What does 'the stringencies of both' add?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's line that we place on the sons the חומרות of כהנים and of ישראלים, and asks what practical law this is for.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says: 'We place on them the stringencies of both.' For what law is this said?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next line of the משנה and asks what it comes to teach. This sets up רב פפא's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה already listed some specific rules for these sons. The גמרא wants to know what extra case this general line covers.

keyTerms.meaning: For what law? What does this teach in practice?

phrases.english: We place upon them the stringencies of, etc.
phrases.notes: The full line is: the חומרות of כהנים and the חומרות of ישראלים.

phrases.english: For what law?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to a new line of the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which practical law the general phrase 'stringencies of both' refers to.

steps.title: רב פפא: their מנחה gets קמיצה but is not eaten
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא says the line refers to their מנחה. A קמיצה is taken from it as with a ישראל, but it is not eaten, as with a כהן.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: it is about their מנחה. A handful is taken from it like a ישראל's מנחה, and it is not eaten like a כהן's מנחה.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא answers the question: the line is about the מנחה these sons bring.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A ישראל's מנחה has a קמיצה taken off, and the rest is eaten by כהנים. A כהן's מנחה is burned completely, with no קמיצה. Since each son might be either one, his מנחה gets the strict side of both: it needs a קמיצה, but it cannot be eaten.

keyTerms.meaning: A handful (קומץ) is taken from it

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said:
For their meal-offering: a handful is taken from it
like the meal-offering of a ישראל,
and it is not eaten
like the meal-offering of כהנים.
phrases.notes: A כהן's מנחה is burned completely, so none of it is eaten.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 19.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Their מנחה follows both sets of חומרות: it needs a קמיצה, and it is not eaten.

steps.title: How is that done?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how both stringencies can be carried out on the same מנחה.
steps.simpleTranslation: How so?
steps.whatsHappening: A short question asking how this works in practice. It sets up the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a קמיצה is taken and the rest cannot be eaten, what is done with the rest? The גמרא wants the practical procedure.

keyTerms.meaning: How so? How is this done?

phrases.english: How so?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks how רב פפא's ruling is carried out.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What happens to the rest of the מנחה.

steps.title: The קומץ and the leftovers are each burned separately
steps.stepSummary: The קומץ is offered by itself, and the שיריים are also burned on their own.
steps.simpleTranslation: The handful is offered by itself, and the leftovers are offered by themselves.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the procedure: both parts go on the מזבח, but separately.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The קומץ is burned, as for a ישראל. The rest cannot be eaten, so it is also burned, but separately from the קומץ. This keeps both חומרות.

keyTerms.meaning: The handful taken from a מנחה and burned
The leftover part of the מנחה

phrases.english: The handful is offered by itself,
and the leftovers are offered by themselves.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 21.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The קומץ is burned on its own, and the שיריים are burned separately.

steps.title: Burning the leftovers breaks בל תקטירו
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects: if part of something already went on the fire, burning the rest is forbidden under בל תקטירו.
steps.simpleTranslation: Read here the rule: anything that has a part that goes to the fire is included in 'you shall not burn'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the procedure from the last step. It looks like it breaks a known rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule is that once the part meant for the fire (here, the קומץ) is burned, offering the other parts on the מזבח is forbidden. That seems to forbid burning the שיריים.

keyTerms.meaning: Read here: apply this rule here
The prohibition 'you shall not burn' (as an offering)

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a separate question from nowhere. It attacks the burning of the שיריים from step 22.

phrases.english: Read here:
anything that has part of it go to the fires,
is included in 'you shall not burn'.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the procedure in step 22.
steps.kashyaTarget: Burning the שיריים separately on the מזבח
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Since the קומץ already went to the fire, burning the rest falls under בל תקטירו.

steps.title: The leftovers go up as wood, like רבי אלעזר
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה son of רבי שמעון בן פזי answers that the שיריים are put on the מזבח only as fuel, following רבי אלעזר.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה son of רבי שמעון בן פזי said: they bring them up as wood, following רבי אלעזר.
steps.whatsHappening: The challenge is answered: the שיריים are not offered as a קרבן, only as firewood.
steps.deeperAnalysis: בל תקטירו forbids offering something as a sacrifice. If the שיריים are put on the fire just as fuel, they are not being offered, so there is no problem. This follows רבי אלעזר's view.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוּדָה בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן פַּזִּי:
phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda, son of Rabbi Shimon ben Pazi, said:
He brings them up as wood,
following Rabbi Elazar.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 23.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining how the act is done
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Burning the שיריים is offering them, which is forbidden.
steps.terutzMaskana: They are burned as fuel, not as an offering.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר: not as a sweet savor, but as wood
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא of רבי אלעזר is brought as the source: the פסוק forbids bringing something up 'for a sweet savor' but allows bringing it up as wood.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was taught: רבי אלעזר says, 'for a sweet savor' you may not bring it up, but you may bring it up as wood.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the source for the answer: רבי אלעזר's reading of the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says these things shall not go up 'לריח ניחח', as a sweet savor. רבי אלעזר reads that as forbidding them only as an offering. Bringing them up as fuel is allowed, and that supports the answer about the שיריים.

keyTerms.meaning: For a pleasing smell: as an offering

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבי אלעזר, the leftovers of the sons' מנחה can be burned separately as wood, so there is no בל תקטירו problem. The next step shows this answer does not work for the רבנן.

phrases.english: As it was taught: Rabbi Elazar says:
'For a sweet savor' you may not bring it up,
but you may bring it up as wood.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source for the answer in step 24.
steps.raayaObject: That something may be put on the מזבח as fuel without counting as an offering
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא of רבי אלעזר on 'לריח ניחח' (ויקרא 2:12)

steps.title: The fuel answer works only for רבי אלעזר
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא points out that burning the שיריים as fuel only works for רבי אלעזר. The רבנן disagree with him, so what would they do?
steps.simpleTranslation: This works well according to רבי אלעזר. But according to the רבנן, what can be said?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer from step 24. That answer depended on רבי אלעזר, and not everyone agrees with him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer was that the שיריים go up on the מזבח only as wood, which רבי אלעזר allows. The רבנן do not allow even that, so for them the problem of בל תקטירו comes back. The גמרא needs a solution that also works for the רבנן.

keyTerms.meaning: This works out well (for one opinion)
What can be said? (what would they answer?)

phrases.english: This works well according to Rabbi Elazar.
phrases.notes: This is the fuel answer from step 24, which comes from רבי אלעזר's ברייתא.

phrases.english: But according to the Rabbis, what is there to say?

steps.triggerLanguage: הָנִיחָא לְרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר. אֶלָּא לְרַבָּנַן, מַאי אִיכָּא לְמֵימַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the תירוץ of step 24 by noting that it depends on one תנא's opinion.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer that the שיריים are burned as fuel, following רבי אלעזר.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The רבנן forbid bringing up leftovers even as wood, so for them the answer does not avoid בל תקטירו.

steps.title: Follow רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון instead
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the procedure follows רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון.
steps.simpleTranslation: The מנחה is handled according to רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a new answer that does not depend on burning the שיריים at all. The source and details come in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Instead of burning the שיריים, we can follow a different תנא, רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון. His method avoids putting the leftovers on the fire, so it gets around the רבנן's objection.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up רבי אלעזר (step 25, about using leftovers as wood) with רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון. They are two different תנאים with two different methods.

phrases.english: That he does it
according to Rabbi Elazar son of Rabbi Shimon.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּעָבֵיד לַהּ כְּרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 26 with a different method.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Switching to a different תנא's procedure that avoids the problem
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The only way to deal with the שיריים is to burn them, which the רבנן forbid.
steps.terutzMaskana: The שיריים do not have to be burned. They can be handled the way רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון describes.

steps.title: The שיריים are scattered on the בית הדשן
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא shows רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון's method: the קומץ is offered alone, and the שיריים are scattered on the place of the ashes.
steps.simpleTranslation: As taught in a ברייתא: רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון says, the קומץ is offered by itself, and the שיריים are scattered on the בית הדשן.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the ברייתא that teaches רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון's method.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The קומץ is burned on the מזבח as usual. The שיריים are not burned and not eaten. They are scattered on the ash pile, which avoids בל תקטירו. It also avoids eating what might be a כהן's מנחה, which may never be eaten.

keyTerms.meaning: The handful taken from a מנחה and burned on the מזבח
The leftover part of the מנחה

phrases.english: As it is taught in a ברייתא:
Rabbi Elazar son of Rabbi Shimon says:
The handful is offered by itself,
and the remainder is scattered on the place of the ashes.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּתַנְיָא, רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source for the answer in step 27.
steps.raayaObject: That there is a method of handling the שיריים without burning them.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא quoting רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון

steps.title: Even the רבנן agree in this case
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן disagree with רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון only about a sinner's מנחה of כהנים, which can be fully offered. In the doubtful case here, even they agree.
steps.simpleTranslation: Even the רבנן disagree with רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון only about a sinner's מנחה of כהנים, since it is fit to be offered. But here, even the רבנן agree.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא removes a possible worry: maybe the רבנן argue with רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון too. It explains that their argument does not apply to this case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A real כהן's חוטא מנחה can be fully burned, so there the רבנן do not scatter the leftovers. Here the person might not be a כהן, so his שיריים cannot be burned. Scattering is the only option, so everyone agrees.

keyTerms.meaning: Fit to be offered on the מזבח

steps.whatToRemember: For a person who may or may not be a כהן, the קומץ is offered by itself and the שיריים are scattered on the בית הדשן. This works for everyone, even the רבנן.

phrases.english: And even the Rabbis do not disagree
with Rabbi Elazar son of Rabbi Shimon
except regarding a sinner's meal-offering of priests,
since it is fit to be offered,
phrases.notes: A real כהן's מנחה is meant to be burned completely, so it can all go on the מזבח.

phrases.english: but here,
phrases.notes: Here means our case, a man who might be a כהן or might not.

phrases.english: even the Rabbis agree.

steps.triggerLanguage: וַאֲפִילּוּ רַבָּנַן לָא פְּלִיגִי עֲלֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Strengthens the answer of steps 27 and 28 by showing that the רבנן accept it in this case.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the scope of the רבנן's disagreement
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The רבנן might argue with רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון, which would leave the problem unsolved for them.
steps.terutzMaskana: The רבנן argue only where the whole מנחה can be offered. In a doubtful case they agree to scatter the שיריים.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The מנחה of a doubtful כהן: the קומץ is offered alone, and the שיריים are scattered on the בית הדשן, according to all opinions.

steps.title: A son whose father is unknown: חליצה but not יבום
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה: a woman remarried within three months and had a son who could be from either husband. Brothers from both husbands do חליצה, not יבום, with his widow. He does the same with theirs.
steps.simpleTranslation: A woman did not wait three months after her husband. She remarried and gave birth, and it is unknown whether the baby is a nine-month baby of the first husband or a seven-month baby of the second. If she had sons from the first husband and sons from the second, they do חליצה and not יבום. Likewise, he does חליצה and not יבום with their wives.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It sets out the case of a son whose father is in doubt and rules on יבום and חליצה between him and his half-brothers.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The son is surely a maternal brother to both sets of sons, but a paternal brother to only one set, and we don't know which. יבום applies only to paternal brothers, and marrying a maternal brother's wife is forbidden. So each side must do חליצה in case they are paternal brothers, but may not do יבום in case they are only maternal brothers.

keyTerms.meaning: A baby born after nine months
A baby born after seven months

steps.confusionAlert: "הוא להם" reverses the case. Now one of the brothers dies childless, and the son of doubtful parentage is the one doing חליצה.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up a new discussion about how a doubt in parentage affects יבום, חליצה and other family laws.

phrases.english: Mishnah:
A woman who did not wait after her husband
phrases.notes: After her husband means after he died or divorced her.

phrases.english: three months, and remarried, and gave birth,

phrases.aramaic: וְאֵין יָדוּעַ אִם בֶּן תִּשְׁעָה לָרִאשׁוֹן
phrases.english: and it is not known whether he is a nine-month baby of the first husband
or a seven-month baby of the last husband,
if she had sons from the first husband
and sons from the second,
they perform חליצה and not יבום.
phrases.notes: The case is that the doubtful son married and died without children, and these brothers face his widow.

phrases.english: And similarly, he toward them:
he performs חליצה and not יבום.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ מִי שֶׁלֹּא שָׁהֲתָה אַחַר בַּעֲלָהּ שְׁלֹשָׁה חֳדָשִׁים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins a new משנה after the previous discussion ends.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When it is unknown which husband fathered a son, he and his half-brothers on both sides do חליצה but not יבום with each other's widows.
